Our K2 ( ages 5 - 6 Years ) young learners embarked on a joyful Noun Detective adventure, discovering that nouns exist everywhere around them! Wearing their detective crowns, they explored classroom and outdoor spaces to collect noun “evidence,” illustrating and labeling their findings to build a vibrant, print-rich environment.

Their hands-on journey continued with the Montessori Moveable Alphabet, where children sorted nouns from storybooks and transcribed them onto four-line cloth. By seamlessly weaving Montessori's tactile, child-led methodology with the IB framework’s inquiry-driven approach, this experience grounded their learning in focused academic rigor while strengthening their vocabulary, phonological awareness, observation, and classification skills.

The excitement grew as they explored common and proper nouns through choosing, sorting, and recording words. This active collaboration nurtured their critical thinking, creativity, and communication, molding them into thoughtful, confident learners.

The real magic happened when children bridged classroom learning with their everyday world, spontaneously spotting nouns in books, posters, and daily conversations. This blend of joyful movement, Montessori-IB synergy, and hands-on mastery ensures strong Grade 1 readiness, proving that when learning is meaningful, it truly comes alive!

We are delighted to welcome Sowmya as our new Head of Learning & Development.

With over 15 years of experience in international education and early childhood development, Sowmya brings to our Kai community enriching expertise in pedagogical leadership, curriculum design, professional development training, teacher mentoring and community engagement. 

Her experiences across IB-PYP and Reggio Emilia beautifully aligns with Kai’s commitment to a child-centred learning environment and experience rooted in play and inquiry.

As Kai continually strives to create a culture of ongoing professional learning through purposeful collaboration, Sowmya will walk alongside our passionate educators to advance our practices for the benefit of every child in our care.

Her approach is a belief that meaningful learning is intentionally nurtured — by educators who remain curious, embrace new perspectives, and create spaces where every child can thrive.

We are thrilled to have her bring her passion and enthusiasm for the Early Years to our Kai community.

Here’s to learning, growing and thriving together.

Rhymes and songs are an integral part of the early years, offering our young Pre Toddlers ( ages 1 - 2 Years ) a creative gateway to experience the world in an imaginary way. During circle time, our Pre-Toddler children enjoyed the rhyme “Alligator, Alligator,” which gently explored friendship and caring for others. 

The children listened with interest, joined in with the repeated lines, and were delighted to wear alligator headgear to bring the story to life.

To build on their enthusiasm, the children created their own alligator artwork by dabbing paint with sponges onto an alligator setup crafted from recycled egg trays. Incorporating repurposed materials served as a wonderful, age-appropriate way to demonstrate recycling and reusing everyday items in creative play. 

This hands-on painting process allowed them to explore colors, patterns, and mark-making while strengthening their fine-motor coordination.

Driven by curiosity, the children then explored the egg trays through touch and movement, feeling the bumpy texture with their hands and walking across the setup to develop sensory awareness and gross-motor skills. Throughout this experience, they demonstrated the IB Learner Profile attributes of Inquirers and Risk-Takers, investigating unfamiliar surfaces with confidence, creativity, and active participation.

At Kai, we believe education flourishes within a connected community, and nurturing meaningful relationships sits at the very core of our ethos. 

To celebrate these extraordinary bonds, our campus recently buzzed with heartwarming energy as we welcomed grandparents into their grandchildren’s daily world for a memorable day dedicated to connection, laughter, and shared experiences. 

The celebration unfolded through a series of engaging, heartfelt moments across the campus. Our Grandparents took center stage during storytelling sessions, captivating young minds with cherished tales from their youth and seamlessly weaving past and present together. 

Creative stations brought generations together on collaborative art projects to craft keepsake pieces built on shared imagination, while interactive sing-alongs and playful movement games had everyone moving, proving that pure joy knows no age limit. 

Watching our children beam with pride as they held hands with their grandparents reinforced the unmatched strength of the village that raises each child. The day left an indelible warmth across our entire community. We extend our deepest gratitude to every grandparent who joined us at Kai, bringing their light, laughter, and wisdom to a celebration that will linger in our hearts for a long time to come.

Stories hold a magical power to spark imagination, turning words into vibrant, hands-on experiences for our youngest learners. 

As part of our How We Express Ourselves Unit of Inquiry, our Toddlers ( ages 2 - 3 Years ) brought the beloved story We’re Going on a Bear Hunt to life through an immersive sensory adventure.

Journeying through swishy grass, deep dark forests, cold water, and thick, oozy mud all set up in our very own open space at Kai, the children enthusiastically chanted, “We’re going on a bear hunt!” as they navigated each setting. This interactive experience nurtured gross-motor skills, coordination, and story sequencing through movement and imaginative play. Throughout the journey, the children shone as Communicators, sharing their excitement through words and gestures, and as Inquirers, curiously discovering what lay around the bend. 

It was a joyful, sensory-rich experience a truly memorable Toddler Wow Moment!

🏆 A Proud Moment for Kai Early Years!

We are delighted to share that Kai Early Years has been recognised as a winner at the India’s Best Design Awards 2026 in the India’s Best Design Project – Spatial Design category!

What makes this recognition particularly special is that Kai Early Years is the only school or education institution among the 2026 winning projects, recognised alongside leading organisations, global brands, architecture practices and innovative businesses from across India.

But for us, this award is about much more than design.

At Kai, we know that the spaces children grow and learn in are an integral part of their experience, shaping how they explore, move, create, connect, feel a sense of belonging and make sense of the world around them.

Our environment has been intentionally designed as a “third teacher", encouraging curiosity and independence, supporting wellbeing, and creating opportunities for children to learn through movement, nature, play and community.

The award jury recognised Kai as a “purpose-built early childhood ecosystem”, designed to rethink how young children experience learning, movement, wellbeing and community.

A heartfelt thank you to educationdesign_international for collaborating with us to bring this vision to life. Together, we have created a space where design begins with a simple but powerful question: What kind of environment do children deserve?

We are deeply grateful to our architects, designers, educators, staff and families who have contributed to bringing the vision of Kai to life, and to the distinguished jury for recognising the thought and purpose behind this space. When we design better spaces for children, we create better possibilities for how they learn, grow and experience the world.

Here’s to creating spaces where little minds can grow, wonder and flourish.

Some flowers say more than words ever could. 🌸🤍

This Teachers’ Day, our Parent School Collaborative (PSC) came together to make our teachers feel truly special — and what better way than with a little bloom, a lot of thought, and the sweetest surprises!

In collaboration with House of Flora, our children got to visit a beautiful Bloom Bar, choose flowers they felt their teacher would love, and watch as they were thoughtfully put together into a beautiful bouquet. 

The best part? Seeing our teachers’ faces light up as the children handed them their carefully chosen blooms. A simple gesture, but one filled with so much love and appreciation. 

The celebrations didn’t stop there! Our PSC parents also organised beautiful flower candles, adding another thoughtful touch to a day dedicated to celebrating the people who make learning so meaningful. 

A heartfelt thank you to House of Flora and our wonderful PSC parents for creating these special moments and reminding our teachers just how much they are valued.

Because sometimes, a little bloom can make someone’s whole day brighter. 

Happy Teachers’ Day to our incredible educators! 🤍

Our K2 learners (Ages 5 - 6 years) have been diving into the fascinating world of mini beasts through the line of inquiry “Types of Mini Beasts.” As young inquirers, they explored four groups, insects, annelids, molluscs and arachnids and began noticing these tiny creatures in their own surroundings.

What made the learning special was the way children connected classroom discoveries to real-life experiences. Conversations about snails, slugs and earthworms sparked thoughtful observations, comparisons and questions, helping build their understanding through meaningful connections.

The children extended their learning through a collaborative Mini Beast Umbrella, where they drew, named and sorted mini beasts into different groups, confidently explaining their thinking. They also transformed simple pebbles into mini beasts, paying close attention to their features while expressing their ideas creatively. Through Bug Art, our young explorers also went on a mini-beast scavenger hunt, collecting leaves and natural materials to create an imaginative mini-beast collage.

What started with tiny creatures has grown into a big learning journey filled with curiosity, discovery, creativity and wonder, inspiring our K2 learners to see the world around them through the eyes of true mini-beast explorer.
